root_cause.text: In the bnxt_en RSS context deletion path (`bnxt_del_one_rss_ctx`), the driver incorrectly gated firmware VNIC/context cleanup on `netif_running(bp->dev)`, so deleting RSS contexts while the interface was down skipped freeing FW resources and caused VNIC leaks and later restoration failures.
root_cause.evidence: The patch removes the `if (netif_running(bp->dev)) { ... }` wrapper around `bnxt_hwrm_vnic_free_one(bp, &rss_ctx->vnic);` and the loop freeing `fw_rss_cos_lb_ctx[]`, and the CVE text says this condition “will make the driver leak VNICs in FW whenever close() happens with active RSS contexts” and that HWRM deletion is safe even when the resource is already freed.

intent_record.intent_summary: Always free RSS VNIC resources during deletion, even when the netdevice is not running.
intent_record.what: The conditional `if (netif_running(bp->dev)) { ... }` wrapper was removed around the RSS VNIC and VNIC context free operations in `bnxt_del_one_rss_ctx()`. The calls to `bnxt_hwrm_vnic_free_one(bp, &rss_ctx->vnic);` and the loop that frees each valid `fw_rss_cos_lb_ctx[i]` entry now execute unconditionally. The later `if (!all) return;` remains unchanged.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the function now attempts to free the RSS VNIC and its associated hardware contexts regardless of whether the network device is currently running. This prevents those resources from being left allocated when teardown happens while the interface is down, ensuring cleanup is performed consistently.

grouping_result.intent: Always free RSS VNIC resources during deletion, even when the netdevice is not running.

relevance_review.reason: The group directly matches the root cause: it fixes RSS context deletion so firmware VNIC/context resources are freed even when the interface is down, preventing the leak caused by gating cleanup on netif_running().

candidates.rationale: This conditional incorrectly prevents RSS VNIC and firmware context cleanup when the netdevice is down, which is the root cause of the resource leak during RSS context deletion.

vuln_statements.explanation: This conditional gates RSS VNIC and firmware context cleanup on the interface being up. When RSS contexts are deleted while the netdevice is down, cleanup is skipped, causing FW resource/VNIC leaks and later restoration failures.

bic_trace_step.reason: The shown function already contains the fix for the reported issue. The vulnerable construct was unconditional FW VNIC/context cleanup in the delete path, but here it is explicitly gated: `if (netif_running(bp->dev)) { bnxt_hwrm_vnic_free_one(...); for (i = 0; i < BNXT_MAX_CTX_PER_VNIC; i++) { ... bnxt_hwrm_vnic_ctx_free_one(...); } }`. This means when the device is down, the code skips FW cleanup and only proceeds with driver-state deletion, matching the commit message: "Support the delete-while-down case. Skip the FW logic and delete just the driver state." Therefore the bug is not present in this version, and the fix is already applied.
